domain: Performance measurement, attribution, reporting and return accountability
executive_summary: Ionic Wealth's ₹500 Cr NDPMS mandate needs one daily-valued, transaction-level TWRR engine that feeds every report — SEBI/APMI filings, client packs and the IC scorecard — with no spreadsheet forks. The design defines a five-tier return hierarchy (R0 paper return through R4 post-tax-liquidation NAV) so alpha (R2 vs a monthly-reset Policy Composite), tax drag (R2-R3, R2-R4) and implementation shortfall (R0-R1) are each measured and owned separately, plus XIRR with the SEBI-mandated min/median/max across IA investors. A three-tier benchmark architecture (T1 APMI Strategy benchmark, T2 Policy Composite, T3 house 80/20 and peer references) keeps the regulatory benchmark distinct from the mandate's true target. Brinson-Fachler attribution (Carino-linked, monthly) decomposes active return by sleeve, with look-through manager and factor attribution for the direct-equity sleeve. Because this is NDPMS, a dedicated implementation-shortfall/consent-latency framework (Perold decomposition) turns the decision-to-execution lag into a budgeted, attributed cost (~15-25 bps p.a. target) rather than an unmeasured drag. A cost-and-tax-drag budget (~97 bps ex-tax, ~45 bps tax) and a worked ₹500 Cr year (gross active +88 bps, net alpha +11 bps after 77 bps of fees) show the fee-hurdle math the IC must internalise. Risk-adjusted metrics carry RAG thresholds feeding a quarterly IC scorecard with named per-line accountability (SAA, TAA, selection, implementation, costs, taxes, valuation quality) — publishing it to clients is the concrete meaning of 'owning the returns.' This sanity-check pass fixed a double-counted implementation-cost term in the annual waterfall, reconciled Table 1's cost wording with the 77 bps fee bridge used elsewhere, corrected a mislabeled 1-sigma claim, and live-verified the three load-bearing regulatory citations (Reg. 22's 3-month reporting ceiling; the 0.50% opex cap, exit-load schedule and high-water-mark rule).

can_do.item: Daily TWRR engine, one cash-flow convention
can_do.what: Build a single daily-valued, transaction-level TWRR engine (start-of-day CF convention, chain-linked) that produces R0-R4 and feeds every downstream report.
can_do.why: SEBI/APMI circular 2022/172 mandates TWRR as the basis for IA performance; a single engine prevents spreadsheet forks and reconciliation breaks across dashboards.
can_do.notes: 2 bp/day swing between start- and end-of-day CF convention on a ₹25 Cr flow shows why the convention must be fixed in policy, not chosen ex post.

can_do.item: Client XIRR with IA min/median/max
can_do.what: Compute money-weighted XIRR per client and, when other investors share the IA, report the min/median/max XIRR across all IA investors.
can_do.why: Explicit SEBI/APMI circular requirement; also the only fair lens on the ₹500 Cr staggered deployment where XIRR and TWRR diverge materially (worked case: TWRR 4.76% vs XIRR 1.17%).

can_do.item: T1 APMI benchmark tagging + 7-working-day filing
can_do.what: Tag the IA to one Strategy (expected Multi Asset), select from APMI's prescribed benchmark list, and file to SEBI/APMI within 7 working days of month-end.
can_do.why: Non-negotiable regulatory floor under SEBI/HO/IMD/IMD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2022/172; a benchmark change requires an exit-load-free exit offer and the old track record must keep being reported.

can_do.item: MF-norm valuation of debt via APMI-empanelled agencies
can_do.what: Value G-sec/SDL/corporate bonds using APMI-empanelled valuation-agency prices on mutual-fund-equivalent norms, with daily accrued interest.
can_do.why: Regulatory requirement; also removes single-source pricing risk on the 22% fixed-income sleeve (~₹110 Cr).

can_do.item: Quarterly client report per Regulation 22
can_do.what: Deliver, within 3 months (verified: Reg. 22 tightened this from the prior 6-month cycle), a signed report covering composition/value, transactions, beneficial interest received, expenses, risks, debt defaults/downgrades and distributor commission.
can_do.why: PMS Regulations 2020 floor; confirmed via live search against current secondary sources this run.

can_do.item: Net-of-fees (R2) as the headline client number
can_do.what: Report R2 (net of PM fee, GST, opex, brokerage/STT/stamp/exchange) as the primary client-facing and SEBI/APMI return; never lead with R0/R1.
can_do.why: Avoids overstating performance and matches SEBI reporting convention; the decision rule anchors alpha accountability on R2 vs the Policy Composite.

can_do.item: Consent-latency log with trade-level time-stamps
can_do.what: Log IC-decision, consent-pack-sent, client-consent and execution timestamps per trade; compute consent-latency, dealing-delay, execution and opportunity-cost lines (Perold shortfall).
can_do.why: NDPMS-specific evidence that the PM acted only on consent, and the only way to attribute the ~15-25 bps p.a. cost of the consent step instead of absorbing it silently into R1.

can_do.item: Benchmark version control
can_do.what: Store every daily benchmark sub-index level with a dated version ID; never back-fill or splice a different series without a footnote.
can_do.why: Protects attribution and alpha history from silent restatement; a house-standard practice extended to the new mandate.

can_do.item: Policy Composite (T2) written into the client agreement
can_do.what: Define the sleeve-weighted Policy Composite (Table 3) as the contractual 'mandate benchmark', reset monthly, reviewed annually with the client.
can_do.why: T1 (APMI benchmark) is a regulatory filing requirement, not necessarily the fair target for a 7-sleeve multi-asset mandate; T2 is what the IC is actually held to.

can_do.item: Brinson-Fachler attribution, Carino-linked, monthly
can_do.what: Decompose active return into allocation/selection/interaction by sleeve each month; chain-link with the Carino factor for the client pack (Menchero acceptable for IC use, pick one and freeze it).
can_do.why: Only way to separate TAA calls from manager/security selection when both are being judged for accountability (worked year: allocation -7 bps, selection +92 bps, interaction +3 bps = +88 bps gross active).

can_do.item: Look-through manager & third-party-PMS attribution
can_do.what: Load AMFI monthly MF holdings and AIF quarterly holdings; attribute manager selection by style tilt vs stock-picking; analyse third-party PMS on custodian holdings exactly like the direct sleeve.
can_do.why: Splits the +44 bps of manager-selection effect into what's genuinely stock-picking skill vs a factor bet, and prevents a third-party manager's own marketing NAV from double-counting fees.

can_do.item: Factor attribution for the direct-equity sleeve
can_do.what: Use the NIFTY-750 scorecard z-scores (quality/growth/value/momentum/macro) plus size/beta to compute holdings-based factor exposures and returns; cross-check with a 36-month regression.
can_do.why: If >60% of 12-month active return is size/momentum, the IC must reclassify it as a style bet (TAA), not manager skill — directly changes the scorecard.

can_do.item: Cost & tax drag budget vs actuals
can_do.what: Track the 8-line cost/tax budget (Table 5: ~97 bps ex-tax/ex-TER/ex-cash-drag + 45 bps tax) against actuals every month, with named owners and escalation triggers per line.
can_do.why: Makes explicit that 88 bps of gross active alpha is barely enough to survive 77 bps of fees — the core fee-hurdle argument for the IC and for fee renegotiation.

can_do.item: R3/R4 post-tax series with deferred-tax-liability marking
can_do.what: Compute post-tax-realised (R3) and post-tax-liquidation (R4, marking unrealised-gain DTL at applicable rate+surcharge+cess) daily, FIFO tax lots per instrument.
can_do.why: Gives a fair 'money in pocket' view and an apples-to-apples comparison across sleeves with very different turnover and embedded tax liability.

can_do.item: Risk-metric RAG dashboard (Table 7)
can_do.what: Publish IR, tracking error, Sharpe/Sortino vs benchmark, max drawdown, Calmar, capture ratios, batting average, TAA hit rate, active share, consent latency and stale-price % with green/amber/red thresholds.
can_do.why: Two consecutive red quarters on any primary metric triggers a formal IC review; red net alpha at 3Y triggers a client-facing strategy review — the metric set is the trigger mechanism.

can_do.item: Quarterly IC scorecard with named owners
can_do.what: Score SAA, TAA, manager selection, security selection, implementation & consent, costs, taxes, and valuation/reporting quality each quarter (-2..+2) against budget, and publish it to the client annually.
can_do.why: This is the concrete mechanism for 'owning the returns' — it ties variable pay and client trust to specific, attributable line items rather than one blended number.

can_do.item: TAA post-mortems with decision-quality classification
can_do.what: Log every TAA call at inception (thesis, size, horizon, exit trigger, expected payoff, stop); at horizon-end classify realised vs counterfactual payoff in a good/bad decision x good/bad outcome matrix.
can_do.why: Separates skill from luck in allocation calls and feeds the TAA hit-rate metric (target ≥55% over trailing 12 calls, payoff ratio ≥1.2); minimum call size ₹5 Cr (1% of AUM) avoids noise trades that only cost latency.

can_do.item: Pre-agreed bands + standing instruction for band-restoring trades
can_do.what: Get client sign-off on ±3% sleeve bands and a standing instruction letting the PM execute band-restoring trades without a fresh per-trade consent cycle.
can_do.why: Directly attacks the 15-25 bps p.a. consent-latency cost that is otherwise unavoidable in NDPMS — but how far a standing instruction can go before it becomes de facto discretionary management is unresolved.
can_do.notes: Confirm scope with compliance against the 16-Jul-2025 Master Circular before relying on it operationally.

can_do.item: GIPS-style composite report and independent verification
can_do.what: Adopt GIPS 2020 calculation and presentation conventions (without claiming certification) and consider third-party verification.
can_do.why: Raises the credibility bar for institutional-style reporting on a ₹500 Cr mandate beyond the SEBI/APMI floor; daily valuation already exceeds the GIPS monthly-minimum requirement.

can_do.item: PME (Kaplan-Schoar) for AIF Cat I/II
can_do.what: Compute Public-Market-Equivalent alongside IRR/TVPI/DPI for AIF Cat I/II holdings, benchmarked to Nifty 500 TRI.
can_do.why: IRR alone cannot be compared to the composite's time-weighted return; PME gives a like-for-like private-vs-public comparison.

can_do.item: Campisi fixed-income attribution
can_do.what: Decompose the fixed-income sleeve's active return into duration, credit spread and carry components.
can_do.why: Sharper than a single Brinson selection number once the FI sleeve (₹110 Cr) grows or turnover rises.

can_do.item: SIF sleeve benchmark
can_do.what: Add a dedicated benchmark and attribution line for Specialized Investment Fund exposure once one is held.
can_do.why: SIF is a new SEBI category (effective 1-Apr-2025, ₹10 lakh PAN-level minimum) the house may allocate into; the benchmark framework should be extensible to it now.

can_do.item: Do not use daily attribution as a decision input
can_do.what: Restrict daily Brinson-Fachler output to monitoring; do not let the IC react to single-day allocation/selection noise.
can_do.why: Daily active-return decomposition is dominated by noise, not signal; trading on it induces exactly the churn NDPMS consent-latency makes expensive.

can_do.item: Do not report the house 80/20 as the mandate's headline benchmark
can_do.what: Keep the house 80% Nifty 50 TRI / 20% Arbitrage index as a T3 reference only; never present it as the client's target benchmark.
can_do.why: The 7-sleeve Policy Composite is expected to trail the house 80/20 by ~1.0-1.5% p.a. in strong equity years and lead in drawdowns — conflating the two would misstate what the IC is managing to.

can_do.item: Do not annualise sub-1-year return periods
can_do.what: Report 1M/3M/6M periods as absolute, not annualised, figures.
can_do.why: Matches SEBI/APMI and GIPS convention; annualising short, volatile periods overstates confidence in the number.

can_do.item: Do not present R0 (paper/model) returns as performance
can_do.what: Use R0 only internally for consent-latency and implementation attribution; never show it to the client or regulator as a return.
can_do.why: R0 excludes real trading, fees and consent delay — showing it as 'performance' would overstate results and could mislead on what NDPMS actually delivered.

can_do.item: Do not charge performance fees on unrealised AIF marks
can_do.what: Compute performance/profit-share fees only on realised gains and against the high-water mark, never on unrealised AIF NAV marks.
can_do.why: SEBI's fee circular ties performance fees to a high-water-mark principle (verified this run); unrealised AIF marks are themselves subject to stale-pricing risk.

can_do.item: Do not change the T1 benchmark without an exit-load-free exit offer
can_do.what: Treat any T1 benchmark change as a regulated event requiring a client exit option with no exit load, and continue reporting the old track record.
can_do.why: Explicit SEBI/APMI circular condition; skipping it would be a compliance breach, not just a reporting inconsistency.

detailed_markdown:
# Performance Measurement, Attribution, Reporting & Return Accountability — ₹500 Cr NDPMS Mandate (Ionic Wealth)

Design date: 2026-09-12. Market context used for calibration: Nifty 50 closed 23,398.10 on 11-Sep-2026 [24]; RBI repo 5.25% (held 5-Aug-2026, SDF 5.00%, MSF 5.50%, stance neutral, FY27 CPI forecast 5.0%) [25][26]; 10Y G-sec approx. 6.97–7.00% in early Sep-2026 [27]. Risk-free rate for ratio metrics: 91-day T-bill, approx. 5.3% (not verified this run — use the RBI/CCIL daily cut-off in production).

## 0. Design principles and regulatory anchors

1. **One engine, many views.** A single daily-valued, transaction-level TWRR engine produces every number in every report (SEBI/APMI filings, client packs, IC scorecards). No spreadsheet forks.
2. **Regulatory floor = SEBI circular SEBI/HO/IMD/IMD-PoD-2/P/CIR/2022/172 (16-Dec-2022, effective 1-Apr-2023)** [1][2]: TWRR is the basis for Investment Approach (IA) performance; XIRR must be presented to each investor along with min/max/median XIRR across all investors in the IA; every IA is tagged to exactly one Strategy (Equity / Debt / Hybrid / Multi Asset); APMI prescribes up to 3 benchmarks per Strategy; a benchmark change requires an exit-load-free exit option and the old track record continues to be reported; marketing/communication must show relative performance vs the selected benchmark and vs other PMs in the Strategy; monthly report to SEBI and APMI within 7 working days of month-end; valuation of debt/money-market per MF norms using APMI-empanelled valuation agencies [1][2][3]. Monthly SEBI/APMI TWRR periods: 1M, 3M, 6M, 1Y, 2Y, 3Y, 4Y, 5Y and since inception [6]. APMI has a standardised ToR for firm-level performance-data audit [5]. Master Circular for Portfolio Managers dated 16-Jul-2025 consolidates these [3] (text not fetched this run — verify paragraph numbers there).
3. **Client reporting floor = PMS Regulations 2020, Regulation 22** [7][8][33]: periodic report to the client at an interval not exceeding 3 months (confirmed — Reg. 22 tightened this from the prior 6-month cycle), covering portfolio composition and value, transactions, beneficial interest received, expenses, risks, defaults/downgrades in debt, distributor commission. Fee/expense rules from SEBI circular SEBI/HO/IMD/DF1/CIR/P/2020/26 (13-Feb-2020, effective 1-Oct-2020): operating expenses ex-brokerage ≤ 0.50% p.a. of average daily AUM (confirmed), exit load ≤ 3%/2%/1% in years 1/2/3 with no exit load after year 3 (confirmed), no upfront fees, performance fee only above high-water mark (confirmed) [10][11][33].
4. **NDPMS specifics.** Non-discretionary/advisory PMs may invest up to 25% of AUM in unlisted securities [9]. Every rebalance needs consent, so *the time between IC decision and execution is a measured, budgeted, attributed cost*. SEBI's 23-Jul-2026 consultation paper (comments closed 13-Aug-2026) proposes overseas investing, pre-IPO/unlisted debt for discretionary PMs, an MF-PMS category and derivative flexibility — proposals only; design for today's rules and keep the benchmark map extensible [12][13].
5. **GIPS 2020 as the quality bar (not a certification claim):** value at least monthly and at every large external cash flow, geometrically link sub-period returns, do not annualise periods < 1 year [14][15]. We exceed the bar with daily valuation.

Feasibility tags used below: **allowed / allowed_with_consent / restricted / not_allowed / unclear_verify**; recommendation tags **MUST / SHOULD / COULD / AVOID**.

## 1. Return computation

### 1.1 Return-series hierarchy (Table 1)

| # | Series | Definition | Costs deducted | Used for | Cadence |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| R0 | Paper / model return | Return of the IC-approved model executed at decision-date closing prices | None | Consent-latency and implementation attribution | Daily |
| R1 | Gross-of-fees TWRR | Actual portfolio at executed fill prices (bid-ask/market impact embedded in the fill, not a separate booked line); MF/ETF TER embedded in NAV | Market impact (bid-ask) + embedded TER only — no PM fee/opex/brokerage booked yet | Attribution vs benchmark; IC scorecard | Daily |
| R2 | Net-of-fees TWRR | R1 minus PM fixed fee, GST on fee, custody/FA/audit/RTA operating expenses (≤ 0.50% cap [10]), and booked brokerage/STT/stamp duty/exchange charges (the explicit contract-note lines, distinct from the bid-ask/impact already inside R1) | All booked fees & expenses (PM fee + GST + opex + brokerage/STT/stamp/exchange) | SEBI/APMI reporting; client headline; alpha accountability | Daily |
| R3 | Post-tax realised TWRR | R2 minus taxes actually paid from the portfolio (STCG/LTCG on realised gains, tax on dividends/interest at slab or TDS) | Fees + cash taxes | Client "money in pocket"; tax-drag attribution | Daily (tax accrued on realisation) |
| R4 | Post-tax liquidation NAV | R3 basis, additionally marking a deferred-tax liability (DTL) on unrealised gains at applicable rates + surcharge + cess | Fees + cash taxes + DTL | Fair comparison across sleeves with different turnover; exit-value planning | Daily |
| X1 | Client XIRR (MWRR) | IRR of all client cash flows and terminal value | Net of fees (state basis) | Mandatory client statement with min/max/median across IA investors [1] | Monthly & quarterly |

Decision rule: **alpha is judged on R2 vs the Policy Composite; tax efficiency is judged on (R2 − R3) and (R2 − R4) vs a tax-drag budget; implementation is judged on (R0 − R1).**

### 1.2 Daily TWRR engine

Sub-period (daily) return with external cash flow CF_t:

r_t = (V_t − V_{t−1} − CF_t) / (V_{t−1} + w·CF_t), with w = 1 if funds/securities are received before 09:15 IST (start-of-day convention), w = 0 if after 15:30 IST (end-of-day convention). Cash flows received intraday default to start-of-day (conservative for inflows). Worked: V_{t−1} = ₹500.00 Cr, CF = +₹25.00 Cr, V_t = ₹527.10 Cr → r = 0.4000% (start-of-day) vs 0.4200% (end-of-day); the 2 bp difference on one day is why the convention is fixed in policy and not chosen ex post.

Chain-linking: TWRR_{0,N} = Π_{t=1..N}(1 + r_t) − 1. Annualise only if N ≥ 365 calendar days: (1 + TWRR)^{365/N} − 1 [15]. Periods < 1 year are reported as absolute (matches SEBI/APMI convention for 1M/3M/6M [6]; verify wording in [3]).

Contributions: sleeve i daily contribution c_{i,t} = w_{i,t−1} · r_{i,t}, where w uses start-of-day market values after cash-flow adjustment; Σ_i c_{i,t} = r_t (cash and accruals are a sleeve). Link contributions across days with the Carino factor (Section 3.1) so they sum to the period TWRR.

Accruals: bond coupon accrues daily (dirty price); dividends accrue on ex-date at gross (pre-TDS) amount in R1/R2 and net in R3; MF IDCW likewise. Fees accrue daily (fixed fee = rate/365 × V_t) and are debited on the billing date as a negative CF for R1 and as an expense for R2 (so R1 is truly gross).

Large cash flows: any external flow ≥ 2% of AUM (₹10 Cr) triggers a mandatory revaluation and a same-day break in the composite; the ₹500 Cr deployment period (first 8–12 weekly tranches) is reported both as a fully-invested TWRR and as an "as-deployed" TWRR with a cash-drag line.

IA aggregation for SEBI/APMI: if the mandate is one IA with several family accounts, IA TWRR is the daily asset-weighted aggregate of all accounts (pool the balance sheet, then apply the formula) — not the average of account TWRRs.

### 1.3 XIRR (money-weighted) client view

XIRR solves Σ CF_k /(1 + IRR)^{d_k/365} = 0 including terminal value. Under the ₹500 Cr staggered deployment, XIRR and TWRR will diverge materially. Worked: ₹250 Cr on day 0, ₹250 Cr at month 6; portfolio +8.0% in H1, −3.0% in H2 → TWRR = 4.76%, XIRR = 1.17%, terminal ₹504.40 Cr. Report both, always with a one-line reconciliation ("timing of your contributions cost/added X% vs the strategy return"). Report the min/median/max XIRR across the IA's investors as required [1]; if the mandate is the only investor in the IA, disclose that fact.

## 3. Attribution

### 3.1 Brinson-Fachler by sleeve, monthly, Carino-linked

Per sleeve i in month t (w = weights, R = returns, B = benchmark, P = portfolio, R_B = total benchmark return):

- Allocation (TAA): A_i = (w_i^P − w_i^B) × (R_i^B − R_B)
- Selection (manager + security): S_i = w_i^B × (R_i^P − R_i^B)
- Interaction: I_i = (w_i^P − w_i^B) × (R_i^P − R_i^B)
- Σ_i (A_i + S_i + I_i) = R_P − R_B exactly for the month.

Linking across months (Carino): k_t = [ln(1+R_P,t) − ln(1+R_B,t)] / (R_P,t − R_B,t); K = [ln(1+R_P) − ln(1+R_B)] / (R_P − R_B); linked effect = Σ_t (k_t / K) × effect_t. Check: two months with (P, B) = (+3.1%, +2.5%) and (−1.8%, −2.2%) → cumulative active 1.00%; linked A = 0.504%, S = 0.495%, I = 0.000%, sum 0.999% (rounding). ### 3.3 Factor attribution — direct-equity sleeve (₹75 Cr, NIFTY-750 scorecard)

Holdings-based (monthly): active exposure to factor k, x_k = Σ_j (w_j^P − w_j^B) z_{j,k} using the scorecard z-scores (quality, growth, value, momentum, macro-sensitivity) plus size and beta; factor return F_k from long-short index proxies: size = Nifty Midsmallcap 400 TRI − Nifty 100 TRI; value = Nifty 500 Value 50 TRI − Nifty 500 TRI; momentum = Nifty 500 Momentum 50 TRI − Nifty 500 TRI; quality = Nifty 200 Quality 30 TRI − Nifty 200 TRI; low-vol = Nifty 100 Low Volatility 30 TRI − Nifty 100 TRI (index names approx. — confirm availability of daily TRI series). Active return = Σ_k x_k F_k (factor) + specific (residual). Returns-based cross-check: regress 36 monthly active returns on the same factor spreads; report R², t-stats, and the residual alpha with its standard error. Decision rule: if > 60% of the sleeve's 12-month active return is explained by size/momentum, the IC classifies it as a *style bet (TAA)* and moves it to the allocation line in the scorecard.

### 3.4 Currency attribution — international sleeve (₹35 Cr)

INR return of a foreign asset: (1 + R_INR) = (1 + R_local)(1 + R_FX). Currency effect = R_FX + R_local × R_FX; local effect = R_local. Because PMS cannot hedge INR exposure via currency derivatives at present (restricted; verify under the 2026 proposals [12]) the currency line is a pass-through, but it must be shown so the IC is not credited/blamed for INR moves. Worked: 7% sleeve, USD/INR +3.0% in the year → +0.21% of portfolio return is FX, not manager skill; if the benchmark is also unhedged INR the effect nets to ≈ 0 in Brinson terms and appears only in the contribution view.

### 3.6 Implementation shortfall and consent-latency attribution (critical for NDPMS)

For each recommended order i with recommended quantity Q_i^rec, executed quantity Q_i^exe, side s_i (+1 buy, −1 sell), decision-date close P_D (IC approval), consent-date close P_C (client consent time-stamp), arrival price P_A (order release to dealer), average fill P_E, and horizon-end price P_H (month-end):

- Consent-latency cost = s_i × (P_C − P_D) × Q_i^exe
- Dealing-delay cost = s_i × (P_A − P_C) × Q_i^exe
- Execution cost (spread + impact) = s_i × (P_E − P_A) × Q_i^exe + explicit charges
- Opportunity cost of unexecuted quantity = s_i × (P_H − P_D) × (Q_i^rec − Q_i^exe)
- Implementation shortfall (Perold) = sum of the four; report in ₹, in bps of AUM and in bps of traded value; also report latency in business days (decision→consent, consent→execution).

### 6.2 IC scorecard (Table 10; quarterly, points-based; example from the worked year)

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| SAA / policy portfolio | IC chair | Composite vs client objective (real return ≥ CPI + 4%, approx.) | ≥ 9.0% | 9.705% | +1 |
| TAA | CIO | Allocation effect; hit rate | ≥ +0.20%; ≥ 55% | −0.065%; 50% | −1 |

Scores feed the team's variable-pay pool (COULD; needs HR design) and are published to the client in the annual review (SHOULD) — publishing the scorecard is the concrete meaning of "owning the returns".

### 6.3 TAA post-mortems

Every TAA call is logged at inception with: thesis, sleeve and size (₹ Cr and % vs policy), horizon, trigger to exit, expected payoff, downside stop. At horizon end: realised payoff vs counterfactual (policy weights) computed by the engine, classified in the decision-quality matrix (good decision/good outcome … bad/bad), latency cost of the call, and a one-paragraph lesson. Quarterly: hit rate, average win/loss, payoff ratio, and correlation of calls with momentum (to detect trend-chasing). Calls smaller than 1% of AUM (₹5 Cr) are not permitted — too small to matter, large enough to cost latency.

## 7. CAN / SHOULD / AVOID summary

- **MUST (regulation or indispensable):** daily TWRR engine with fixed cash-flow convention; XIRR with min/median/max across IA investors; T1 APMI benchmark tagging and monthly filing within 7 working days; MF-norm valuation via APMI-empanelled agencies for debt; quarterly client report with the regulation's contents; net-of-fees reporting; consent-latency log with time-stamps (NDPMS evidence and attribution); benchmark version control.
- **SHOULD (first 6 months):** Policy Composite in client agreement; Brinson-Fachler with Carino; look-through manager attribution; factor attribution for direct sleeve; cost & tax drag budget; R3/R4 post-tax series with DTL; risk-metric RAG dashboard; IC scorecard; TAA post-mortems; pre-agreed bands + standing instruction (after compliance confirms scope).
- **COULD:** GIPS-style composite report and independent verification; PME for AIFs; Campisi fixed-income attribution; SIF sleeve benchmark once a SIF is held (SIF minimum ₹10 lakh at PAN level, effective 1-Apr-2025 [30][31]).
- **AVOID:** daily attribution as a decision input (noise); reporting the house 80/20 as the headline benchmark; annualising < 1-year returns; presenting model/paper returns as performance; performance fees on unrealised AIF marks; changing T1 benchmark without an exit offer; estimating AIF/international NAVs in-house; equal-weighting account TWRRs for the IA.

risks_and_pitfalls: Consent latency is the structural NDPMS risk: every rebalance needs client sign-off, so the ~15-25 bps/year implementation-shortfall budget can blow through if consent SLAs slip — this must be monitored daily, not discovered at quarter-end.

Reporting the house 80% Nifty 50 TRI / 20% Arbitrage benchmark as the mandate's headline number would misstate the target — the 7-sleeve Policy Composite is expected to trail it by ~1.0-1.5% p.a. in strong equity years, which could look like underperformance when it is by design.

77 bps of fees against 88 bps of gross active return leaves only +11 bps of net alpha — a small forecasting error or a single weak quarter of manager selection can flip the mandate from a fee success to a fee-refund conversation.

Whether a pre-agreed model + ±3% bands + standing instruction can be relied upon without becoming discretionary management (and thus a licensing/registration problem) is explicitly unclear_verify in the source design; operating on an unconfirmed reading of the regulations is a compliance risk.

AIF Cat I/II valuations are only independently struck every 6-12 months; a 5-10% haircut rule on stale marks is a policy choice, not a regulatory number, and disagreements with the AIF manager's own NAV could create client-facing valuation disputes.

The DTL (deferred tax liability) computation on R4 depends on surcharge slabs and holding-period classification that are client-specific; using a single illustrative 15% surcharge across all clients would misstate the liquidation NAV for clients in a different tax bracket.

Section 50AA slab taxation of debt MFs bought on/after 1-Apr-2023, and the FY2025-26 narrowing of the 'specified MF' definition to >65% debt funds, must be applied fund-by-fund; misclassifying a hybrid/multi-asset scheme here would misstate R3/R4 materially.

Third-party PMS is valued on custodian holdings, not the manager's own statement; if custodian data lags or is incomplete, the 0.10% NAV-gap escalation threshold could be breached silently for months in an AIF-heavy or PMS-heavy period.

Because the mandate is NDPMS, if the only investor in the IA is this client, the SEBI-mandated min/median/max XIRR disclosure across IA investors degenerates to a single number — failing to disclose that fact explicitly could look like a compliance omission even though it is technically correct.

A benchmark change (T1) without the required exit-load-free exit offer is a clear regulatory breach, but the operational trigger for that step (who initiates the exit offer, on what timeline) is not defined in the design and needs a named owner before go-live.

The worked ₹500 Cr numbers throughout the document are illustrative, not forecasts; if the IC or client mistakes the +11 bps net-alpha worked example for a target rather than a hurdle illustration, expectations will be miscalibrated from day one.

Primary regulatory texts ([1] the Dec-2022 circular, [3] the Jul-2025 Master Circular, [7][8] the PMS Regulations and FAQ) were identified via search excerpts, not fetched and read in full this run — paragraph-level details (e.g., exact wording on 3-month reporting, benchmark-change mechanics) should be verified against the primary PDFs before this design is finalised operationally.

The 25% unlisted-securities limit for non-discretionary/advisory PMs [9] is sourced from a secondary (Mondaq) summary, not the regulation text itself, and was not independently re-verified this run — confirm the exact regulation clause before using it as an investment constraint.

SEBI's 23-Jul-2026 consultation paper proposals (overseas investing, pre-IPO/unlisted debt, MF-PMS category, derivative flexibility) are proposals only; designing around them as if final would create rework risk and, if acted on prematurely, a possible regulatory breach.
open_questions: Can a signed standing instruction for band-restoring trades within ±3% sleeve bands be executed without a fresh per-trade consent cycle, or does that cross into discretionary management under the current (or 16-Jul-2025 Master Circular) regulations? Needs a compliance ruling before the consent-latency mitigation in §3.6 can be relied on operationally.

Whether a custom T2 Policy Composite may be shown alongside the mandatory T1 APMI benchmark in client-facing marketing/communication materials, or whether only T1 may be shown in that context — flagged unclear_verify in the source design.
Whether NDPMS IAs are included in APMI's published peer-group TWRR tables for quartile ranking, which affects whether the peer-comparison panel (Table 9) can be populated at all for this mandate.

What is the firm's actual PM fee rate for this ₹500 Cr NDPMS mandate — the design uses an illustrative 0.50% (typical range 0.25-0.75% approx.); the real negotiated rate changes every downstream fee/alpha-hurdle number in Tables 5, 10 and the worked examples.

What is the confirmed current APMI benchmark list for the Multi Asset Strategy (or whichever Strategy this IA is tagged to), since T1 selection is a hard regulatory requirement and the design currently assumes 'Multi Asset' as expected rather than confirmed.

Is direct-plan-only investment in mutual funds mandatory for PMS accounts under current rules (flagged 'verify' against the Master Circular in Table 5's TER line), and does that constrain the active-MF sub-sleeve's fund selection universe?

What is the client's actual tax status (surcharge slab, residency, any DTAA considerations) needed to correctly parametrise the R3/R4 tax and DTL calculations, rather than the illustrative 15% surcharge used in the worked example?
How will the firm source and validate a daily risk-free rate (91-day T-bill cut-off) in production, given the design used an unverified approx. 5.3% for calibration only?
What is the operational process and named owner for triggering an exit-load-free exit offer if the T1 benchmark ever needs to change, and how will that be tracked to closure?

Should the IC scorecard (Table 10) actually feed the team's variable-pay pool, and if so, who in HR owns designing that link — the design flags this as 'could, needs HR design' but does not resolve it.
At what AUM or holding threshold does a SIF allocation become likely enough to warrant building the SIF benchmark and attribution line now, versus deferring until a SIF position is actually taken?

Will the firm pursue GIPS composite verification (independent, third-party) for this mandate, given it is flagged only as a 'could' — this affects whether marketing can reference GIPS-consistent claims at all.
